title: Fix or quarantine the flaky SynchronousIoCancelTests
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

retry-cancel-loop-clears-flake-without-collateral: needs first: Something has to keep the resend alive while one CancelSynchronousIo call is held in the kernel: for example, each attempt issued from its own short-lived thread or timer callback, so a …

If SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel (failed once in a full-suite run beside the unserialized repro, message never captured) recurs after the fix and the serialization, is it part of SL-055 or a separate slice?

If a second concurrent CancelSynchronousIo turns out not to free a re-blocked wait, no fix inside the current design can make the repro pass. Is quarantining the flaky test and the repro, with a tracked lost-cancel defect left open, an accepted outcome for this slice, or does it stay blocked until a real fix exists?
A fresh dedicated thread per attempt versus a small fixed set of long-lived attempt threads. Uncontested here; the proposal chose the simpler per-attempt thread.
Cap of 4 in-kernel attempts versus 2 or unbounded. 4 was chosen as margin over the theoretical 2.
Gate and drain as a Monitor-based lock versus a counted event or SemaphoreSlim. Left to the build.
Recording the '>2 s under load' answer as a code comment and slice record versus a docs page or ADR.
The repro stays its own test class with its own serialized collection, rather than being folded into SynchronousIoCancelTests.

C-011 (delivered-cancel latency over 2 s) and C-012 (Thread.Start throwing) have no dedicated test. The design marked both non-material. That is unchanged by this attempt, and nothing owed asks for them.
.taad/fitness.yaml has no conflict markers left but is still marked UU in the index, because this build does not stage or commit. The engine has to `git add` it when it commits the merge.

The concentrated loaded pass takes about 100 s per class run (test process and 4 busy threads pinned to CPUs 14-15). So the design's 30-run loaded protocol cannot fit the 'a few minutes per loaded pass' machine rule in one pass. Validate needs to split it across several passes, or run fewer.

attempts.head: 5654d9b2979db5964482574059927f0595467ba1
attempts.summary: This slice fixed a genuine lost-cancel race in SynchronousIoCancel.CancelLoop: the single canceller thread could get stuck inside a blocking CancelSynchronousIo call once the target thread re-blocked, silently killing the 25 ms resend and leaving guarded I/O blocked indefinitely under load.
